findings.problem: The fourth interpretation says: 'Sicard of Cremona repeats the reading for the Mass that he and Rupert knew, whose Gospel was Christ's entry into Jerusalem (Mt 21; Mitrale V).' The three-document profile, Liturgical commentators (guidance/liturgy/propers-three-documents.md L288-298), allows a commentator's other Gospel to be recorded in research/scope.md and 'in at most one clause of the expansive study's scope appendix', and says: 'The readings, the concise study and the homily do not mention his other Gospel, his other chants or the Mass they belonged to: a 1962 guide is not the place for other Masses.' The scope appendix already carries that one clause (90 L75-77, 'Rupert and Sicard expound a Mass of this Sunday whose Gospel was another'). The sentence in lane 4 is new this iteration; it follows the second of the two rewrites that STU-019 offered, which the profile does not permit. The Sicard and Rupert readings it reports are accurate: Sicard's first-Sunday chapter gives the Virgin reading of the Communion (terra nostra, id est beata virgo concipiens, PL 213, Mitrale V), and Rupert's is quoted correctly from De div. off. III.2. Lane 3 L138-141 and lane 4 L146-149, which cite Sicard 'writing of the churches that read this Gospel' / 'for the churches that read this Mass's Gospel, Erunt signa', are not affected: they report Sicard's own Erunt signa paragraph, which does set the Epistle and Communion beside this Gospel, and they name no other Gospel or Mass.
findings.required_result: Remove the clause that names the other Mass and its Gospel, so that the sentence reads: 'Sicard of Cremona repeats the reading (Mitrale V).' Name no other Gospel, chant or Mass anywhere in the interpretations, the comparison or the opening; leave the one clause in the scope appendix (90 L75-77) as the study's only mention.

findings.problem: The Alleluia's contribution to the second interpretation rests on a shared verb and stops there. After 84.9 (sons of God sed per fidem ... nondum sumus in re) and 1 Jn 3:2 (nondum apparuit quid erimus), the paragraph says 'The verb is the one he used in the letter to Hesychius, where the Church "will not appear" when the persecutors rage' (Ep. 199.39, Ecclesia non apparebit, checked) and ends 'In the letter she may be lost to sight in persecution; in the sermon those who sing the verse have not yet appeared as what they will be.' The verb is in St John's sentence, which Augustine quotes, not in the Alleluia, and the two passages are left side by side as a balanced pair without the reason they bear on each other or on this interpretation (guidance/editorial.md L400-405: a reviser 'replaces it with the plain connection it was gesturing at ... and does not leave the quotations side by side'; propers-three-documents.md L228-229 on quotations sharing a word). Isolated instance.
findings.required_result: State what the Alleluia gives this interpretation in plain words, or drop the verb link. For example: 'Those who sing it are the Church in her present age: sons of God already, by faith, and not yet what they will be, as the coming Ambrose and Augustine find in her is already under way and not yet complete.' If the link to Ecclesia non apparebit is kept, say what follows from it, e.g. 'The Church that persecution hides in the letter is the same company whose glory, in the sermon, has not yet appeared.'

findings.location: sections/20-lift-up-your-heads.tex L86-88, L96, L208; sections/30-coming-through-the-church.tex L208-210, L240; sections/40-hour-to-rise.tex L97-101, L100, L130-132, L138, L144, L158; sections/50-mercy-shown-salvation-given.tex L173-178
findings.problem: Small slips of attribution and wording in sentences rewritten for STU-015 and STU-019, checked against the sources. (a) 20 L86-88: 'Paul's night and Gregory's road ask the same of the hearer: to hurry as the end draws near, and not to grieve at it as the friend of the world does.' Paul says nothing of grief at the end; the friend of the world is Gregory's (I.1.3, Jas 4:4), and the qualification 'on Gregory's account' that STU-015's rewrite carried was dropped. (b) 20 L96: 'Gregory draws the same lesson from the parable of the fig tree' now follows the Alleluia paragraph, so 'the same lesson' has no antecedent; Gregory introduces the parable as showing quod calcari mundus ac despici debeat (I.1.3). (c) 30 L208-210: 'That is a coming in the present, by the commandments and the counsels'. Aquinas says Per has enim vias venit dominus ad nos, maxime per praeceptum caritatis, of the ways that are the precepts; the counsels are the paths, and he does not say the Lord comes by them (Super Ps. 24 n. 4). (d) 40 L98-99: 'His question in Latin is quis me liberaret'. The Latin reads miserum ergo me quis liberaret de corpore mortis huius (Conf. VIII.5.12), and the question is St Paul's in Rom 7:24, which Augustine makes his own; the reader is not told so, in a lane about Romans. (e) 40 L130-132: 'Aquinas's trust "through Christ" says where the lifting comes from.' Aquinas distinguishes two preparations for prayer, the lifting of the mind per contemplationem ... et per amorem and the trust (fiducia) of in te confido, and cites 2 Cor 3:4-5 for the trust only (Super Ps. 24 n. 1); the sentence moves the study's inference into his citation. (f) 50 L176-178: 'The one the Secret asks to receive worthily at the altar' credits the Secret with Schuster's paraphrase (p. 322); the Secret asks that the holy things bring us purer ad suum principium. (g) Refrains: the Secret's sentence opens 'At the offering the Secret asks' in three lanes (20 L208, 30 L240, 40 L158), and lane 3 links four times in thirty lines by 'the same' (L100 'the same verb and ... the same deliverer', L138 'with the same verb', L144 'the same danger', L158 'of the same kind').
findings.required_result: (a) 'In this Mass Paul's night and Gregory's road ask the same of the hearer, to hurry as the end draws near; Gregory adds that only the friend of the world grieves to see it come.' (b) 'Christ's parable of the fig tree, Gregory says, shows that the world is to be trodden underfoot and despised.' (c) 'That is a coming in the present, by the commandments and above all the commandment of charity, and it is the kind of coming ...' (d) 'His question is St Paul's (Rom 7:24) in his own Latin, miserum ergo me quis liberaret, "who would set me, wretched as I am, free?", and the Collect's last words use the same verb ...' (e) 'Sung after Paul's command, the Offertory's lifted soul is the opposite of that weight, and its next words, in te confido, are the trust that Aquinas, with St Paul, places in God through Christ and not in ourselves.' (f) 'Schuster reads the request as a prayer that "we may worthily receive him who is its Author" (p. 322); the Author received would be the Christ whom the Alleluia asked God to give.' (g) Vary the Secret's opening in two of the three lanes (e.g. 30 L240 'Over the gifts the Secret asks for the cleansing that would take that obstacle away'), and recast two of lane 3's 'same' links (e.g. L144 'Christ and Paul both warn against a heart dulled by excess when the day arrives'; L158 'the Secret asks God for that cleansing').

findings.problem: 'It shares with the third a view toward Christmas, but where the third prepares the hearer for a feast, the fourth asks for Christ himself' sets the fourth interpretation against a position the third does not hold. The third also asks for Christ: its Collect asks the Son to come and set us free (40 L97-101), its Alleluia asks for the nearer salvation as God's gift (40 L147-149), and its allegorical sense, with Aquinas, makes that salvation Christ in his first coming (40 L190-192). The real difference is what each turns on: the hearer's waking, or the gift asked for though already given. Isolated instance.
findings.required_result: State the difference the two interpretations actually have, e.g.: 'It shares with the third a view toward Christmas. The third turns on the hearer's waking and asks Christ to set the sleeper free; the fourth turns on the gift itself, Christ asked for although he has been given, given once as man and to be given as God.'

findings.problem: Unchanged since study review 1. The research record still says that the verb the Epistle addresses to us (surgere) the Collect asks God to exercise. The Collect's verbs are excita and veni. The study no longer reasons so (40 L9-13, L97-101; 60 L22-25); the row is not reader-facing.
findings.required_result: When research is next re-entered, rewrite the row to say what the Collect asks: Christ is asked to stir up his power and come, so that we are snatched from danger te protegente and saved te liberante. Record the link the study actually draws (Augustine's miserum ergo me quis liberaret, Conf. VIII.5.12, and the Collect's te liberante), and remove the surgere claim.

summary: Cold review, iteration 2, of the expansive study src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/01-first-sunday-of-advent/main.tex: every section file read whole (00 and 05 for context; 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 90, generation-metadata.tex and research/production-review.md as the REVIEW_SCOPE), the generated Scriptural Date and Location appendix not reviewed as prose. Appointed-text mode is 'complete' in proper-components.toml, agreeing with research/context.md, research/scope.md, propers/verified.md and the production plan (Claude authorization of 2026-11-25; no reference-only authorization), so the label is Full PDF and the reference-only checks do not apply. STU-015 is repaired: every listed disclaimer is gone, the rotating join formulas and the 'On X's reading' family are gone, and each cross-text link is now stated once where it is drawn, by varied means (the order of the Mass, a conditional, a shared word, a plain comparison). STU-016 and STU-018 are repaired; the study side of STU-019 is repaired. Evidence checked at the cited loci, quotation by quotation: Gregory, Hom. in Ev. I.1.1-6 (tracked Wikisource text); Augustine, Ep. 199.1-3, 25-27, 34-45 and 54, En. in Ps. 24.1-4 and 24.10, and Confessions VIII.5.12 Latin (augustinus.it and The Latin Library pages refetched into the worker scratch area, SHA-256 matching the registered 5b570f96..., 614fe703... and be90ce92...), Confessions VIII.5.12 NPNF English, En. in Ps. 84.9 and 84.15 (tracked Latin); Aquinas, Super Rom. 13 l. 3 and Super Ps. 24 nn. 1-4 (corpusthomisticum pages refetched, hashes matching 1c3db878... and 5e8fdbbe...); Ambrose, Expos. in Luc. X.37-42; Cyril of Alexandria, sermon 139 (Payne Smith); Cyril of Jerusalem, Cat. 15.1, 15.3, 15.4; Chrysostom, Hom. in Rom. 24 on vv. 11-14 and Hom. in Mt. 77; Bede on Lk 21:32-33; Bellarmine on Ps 24 and Ps 84 at the verses cited; Rupert, De div. off. III.2, Sicard, Mitrale V (including the Erunt signa paragraph, PL 213 col. 205-206 in the OCR) and Durandus, Rationale VI, in the tracked OCR; Schuster pp. 321-323 in the tracked machine text. Every quotation checked matches its witness. Consequential-difficulty test, by locus and outcome: lane 1, Gregory I.1.3 (levate capita, id est exhilarate corda; Jas 4:4; Quid est vita mortalis, nisi via?) and I.1.6 (praecones ... judex) against Augustine Ep. 199.34-37, 54: taught, the inference intelligible. Lane 2, Augustine Ep. 199.34-39 (portents no greater than before Christ; the evils common utrique regno; Ecclesia est enim sol et luna et stellae; Ecclesia non apparebit) and 199.26, 41-42, 45 (the coming in corpore suo, quod est Ecclesia; the cloud; the daily coming), with Ambrose X.37-39: taught. Lane 3, Aquinas, Super Rom. 13 l. 3 (duplex propinquitas; secundum quod Ecclesia haec verba adventus tempore legit; tempus misericordiae; the three nights): taught. Lane 4, Augustine En. in Ps. 84.9 (dedit ... hominem ... daturus est Deum) and 84.15 against Bellarmine on Ps 84 expl. 12 (the untouched virgin land): taught. Each interpretation engages all ten texts, carries its own four senses, and has two carrying authors with developed reasoning. Limits: no print export built or inspected; mechanical gates not rerun (the engine's study-preflight iteration 2 is recorded PASS); Schuster read only in the tracked machine text; the appointed Latin and English (section 05, unchanged) not re-collated; the earlier forms of the rewritten sentences were available to me only as STU-015 quotes them, so their attribution was checked against the sources. Verdict CHANGES_REQUIRED: one blocking finding (STU-020: the fourth interpretation names the Gospel and Mass of Rupert's and Sicard's Sunday, which the three-document profile bars from the interpretations), with three new advisories (STU-021 to STU-023) and the two research-owned advisories STU-017 and STU-019 carried forward unchanged in substance.
